summary.text: An 87-year-old man with heart failure with preserved ejection fraction, chronic kidney disease, hypertension and cerebellar infarction presented in 2022 with worsening renal function and hypercalcemia. Serum calcium was elevated at 2.99 mmol/L with a markedly elevated intact PTH of 505.1 pg/mL, a 24-hour urine calcium of 304.8 mg/day and a high calcium clearance ratio, leading to a diagnosis of primary hyperparathyroidism.

Bone mineral density showed osteopenia and renal sonography a small left renal stone. A neck ultrasound identified no parathyroid lesion, but sestamibi SPECT/CT showed a tracer-avid lesion in the left superior anterior mediastinum, excised by video-assisted thoracoscopic surgery. Histology showed an ectopic parathyroid gland with hyperplasia that was PTH-positive on immunohistochemistry, and serum calcium normalized during follow-up.

Two years after the prior episode he presented with generalized weakness, drowsy consciousness and abdominal distension, with muscle strength 4/5 in all extremities. Calcium was 3.31 mmol/L, creatinine 2.91 mg/dL with acute kidney injury, and intact PTH suppressed at 9.3 pg/mL. CT showed a 12.8 cm pelvic mass; biopsy with immunohistochemistry confirmed a GIST staged cT4N0M0, stage IIIA, and malignancy-associated hypercalcemia was strongly suspected.

He received intravenous fluids, furosemide and calcitonin, but hypercalcemia was incompletely resolved with corrected calcium 3.02 mmol/L. Following pathological confirmation of GIST, a single dose of subcutaneous denosumab 120 mg and imatinib 100 mg daily were given on the same day. Calcium normalized two weeks later and a transient PTH rise from hypocalcemia returned to normal with calcium supplementation. After three months normocalcemia persisted without supplementation, tumor size fell to 8.8 cm and no clinically significant adverse effects occurred.
